title: Apartment Interior Design 45 m² | DUMSKAYA DESIGN
description: 45 m² apartment: interior design. DUMSKAYA DESIGN, Bratislava and Vienna.

parts.html: An interior design project for a 45 m² apartment in a contemporary style. The task was to fit in all the necessary zones while keeping a small apartment visually light and not wasting a single meter. We built the interior on three materials: light oak, smooth fronts in the gray-beige tone of the walls, and light stone-look tiles. Almost all the storage is hidden in built-in furniture.

The kitchen, dining area, and living room share one room with access to the balcony. The kitchen runs along the end wall: the base units and the oven column are light gray and handleless, the upper cabinets are oak veneer, and the backsplash is stone-look tile. A round oak table with four upholstered chairs separates the kitchen from the sofa without any partitions. Above the table hangs a wide, flat pendant; the rest of the light comes from surface-mounted spotlights.

Opposite the sofa is a TV wall with a floating media unit and open oak shelving. Along the long wall from the living room to the entrance hall run floor-to-ceiling cabinets with fronts in the wall color: they hardly read as furniture, yet they hold a lot.

Behind the bed, a light veneer panel spans the full width of the wall, with vertical slats in the center and the bedside tables hung from it. Opposite stands a built-in unit in the same oak: floor-to-ceiling cabinets at the sides and a niche between them with a desk, drawers, and a TV. The workspace fit into the bedroom, so a separate study wasn’t needed.

In the bathroom, the walls and floor are large-format tiles that look like porous light stone. There is a round mirror with perimeter lighting, a countertop basin on an oak vanity, a wall-hung toilet, and a tall cabinet next to it. The entrance hall has a floor-to-ceiling wardrobe with a dark profile handle and a full-height mirror on the opposite wall that makes the passage look wider.

The kitchen, cabinets, TV wall, headboard, work unit, and bathroom vanity were sized for this apartment. This is custom furniture: the cabinets reach exactly to the ceiling and meet the walls with no gaps.
